    "summary": "fix(1568): sm-merge-guard covers by tree, not merge-sha",
    "description": "## The false alarms

Two sm-guard alarms in 49 minutes, both on SM train merges whose trees were **proven byte-identical** to their green validations:

| push (main) | merge of | validated by | proven identical tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| `392fe540ae73` @14:43:44Z (#1568 body) | #1484 | run [38260860862](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38260860862) (head `06898ec2b58c`, green 14:09Z) | `0fd92616c897199580c030675dd7854758ea9879` — `git rev-parse '<sha>^{tree}'` equal on both |
| `afed64bfd07a` @15:30:51Z (#1568 comment) | #1468 | run [38267190833](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38267190833) (head `d9b302c6b4d7`, green 15:01Z) | `265cec3014449d6c32fe7d15cad4403d4fb346eb` — equal on both |

gh-1537 AC5's tree-coverage intent was already implemented — the guard passes `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` and `decide()` compares it against each dispatch run's head tree. Two wiring bugs killed it.

## Mechanism (two bugs, both in `fetch_validated_runs`)

1. **Wrong jq path.** Each run's tree was resolved via `gh api repos/.../commits/<sha> --jq .tree.sha` — but the commits API has **no top-level `tree` key** (keys: `author, comments_url, commit, committer, files, html_url, node_id, parents, sha, stats, url`); the tree lives at `.commit.tree.sha`. The lookup returned empty, `tree_sha` stayed falsy, and the tree-match branch never fired → **every merge-commit landing alarmed** (only exact-SHA fast-forwards could pass).
2. **`conclusion` dropped from fetched runs.** `decide()` re-checks `run.get("conclusion") != "success"` on every run — a defensive re-check for the `--runs-json` test seam — but the fetch path never put `conclusion` in the dicts, so every live run read as `None != "success"` and was skipped → **the live path alarmed on every push**, even the fast-forward case. The Dart fixtures all carry `conclusion: 'success'`, which is why the test seam never saw it.

## Fix (surgical)

- `.tree.sha` → `.commit.tree.sha` (+ `or None` normalization)
- propagate `conclusion` into fetched run dicts
- the alarm body's "considered runs" lines now render each run's **resolved tree** alongside the head sha, so future alarms are self-diagnosing

## Live verification (read-only, post-fix)

- merge `392fe540ae73` / tree `0fd92616…` → `ok — tree match: run 38260860862 validated this exact tree` (exit 0)
- merge `afed64bfd07a` / tree `265cec30…` → `ok — tree match: run 38267190833 validated this exact tree` (exit 0)
- synthetic uncovered tree → alarm, exit 3 (the invariant still bites)

## Offline test matrix — `scripts/sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh` (16 checks, wired into ci.yml)

PATH-stubbed `gh` serving the **real** commits-API response shape (tree nested under `commit`, no top-level `tree`), real shas from the #1484 false alarm:

- **AC1** (regression) merge-commit landing with identical tree validates; verdict cites the covering run
- **AC2** uncovered tree → alarm, exit 3
- **AC3** fast-forward (pushed sha == validated head) validates, no tree lookup needed (fixture 404s)
- **AC4** race: a validation still `in_progress` at push time can never certify → alarm
- **AC5** tree-lookup failure (commit API 404) → warning + alarm, never a false validate
- **AC6** alarm body renders considered runs' resolved trees and files with `bug`+`sm-guard` labels (dedup convention untouched)

## Race decision (AC4): alarm stands, no wait/recheck

The invariant is "validated **before** merge"; only a completed-success run certifies. The SM merges strictly after green, so a run still in progress at push time means the merge beat its validation — that *is* the violation. A recheck-wait would contradict the guard's design (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly not a polling backstop) and would delay-then-mask real violations; the deduplicated issue keeps the evidence if the run lands green afterward.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: both fixes + self-diagnosing alarm body + fixture selftest in CI. Unchanged by design: 24h window, `MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS=40`, release-bump skip, alarm dedup/labels.

Fixes #1568"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry

  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND

  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SM merge guard (gh-1537 AC5) — the cheap alarm for the serialized-
validation invariant.

Invariant under watch: the SM queue (machine-sm.yml -> factory-sm) is
strictly serialized and validates the EXACT tree that merges — update
branch onto main, dispatch ci.yml on the updated head, merge only when
green. With the post-merge main CI run retired (gh-1537), nothing else
stands between a violated invariant and a red main: this guard fires on
every push to main and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a
SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch run (an SM pre-merge validation).

A push whose tree has no successful dispatched validation is the
#687-invariant violation the owner asked to alarm on instead of relying
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard —
defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full
quality gate that runs on the cut v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ALARM_LABEL = "sm-guard"
# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, window_hours: int) -> list:
    """Recent SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch runs, each with the tree
    sha of its head commit resolved via the commits API."""
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", "ci.yml",
             "--event", "workflow_dispatch",
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append({
            "database_id": r["databaseId"],
            "head_sha": r["headSha"],
            # decide() re-checks conclusion on every run; without the
            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below
            "created_at": r["createdAt"],
        })
    # Newest first — the match is almost always the first lookup.
    for run in runs[:MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS]:
        try:
            # The commits API nests the tree under `commit` — `.tree.sha`
            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()
            run["tree_sha"] = tree or None
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    return runs


def decide(subject: str, pushed_sha: str, pushed_tree: str,
           runs: list) -> dict:
    """The pure invariant check. `runs` carry head_sha/tree_sha of
    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
        return {"verdict": "skipped",
                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
    for run in runs:
        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
        # invariant holds by construction).
        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
                              f"commit re-landed it)"}
    return {"verdict": "alarm",
            "reason": "no successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run covers "
                      "this tree — the SM merged without (or before) a "
                      "green validation of the exact tree"}


def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
                runs: list) -> None:
    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
    links = "\n".join(
        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
        + ")"
        for r in runs[:10])
    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
    body = (
        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
    if existing.strip():
        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
           "--body", body)

    else:
        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push would skip the guard (defense-in-depth —
# gh-1522 retired the bump flow, so none land anymore; if one ever
# returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the v* tag run's full
# quality gate BEFORE publish/binaries). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Pin to the SAME frozen identity PUSHED_SHA uses
          # (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha): the tree under
          # assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD, so an unpinned
          # checkout could drift to a moved main and have run-for-push-A
          # certify a newer push B's tree it never examined (same lesson
          # as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin,
          # #1178 — gh-1522 folded tag cutting back into the release job).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --alarm-issue

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1569
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1569
- **Title**: fix(1568): sm-merge-guard covers by tree, not merge-sha
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1568-sm-guard-tree-coverage` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T15:51:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T16:00:44Z

## PR Description

## The false alarms

Two sm-guard alarms in 49 minutes, both on SM train merges whose trees were **proven byte-identical** to their green validations:

| push (main) | merge of | validated by | proven identical tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| `392fe540ae73` @14:43:44Z (#1568 body) | #1484 | run [38260860862](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38260860862) (head `06898ec2b58c`, green 14:09Z) | `0fd92616c897199580c030675dd7854758ea9879` — `git rev-parse '<sha>^{tree}'` equal on both |
| `afed64bfd07a` @15:30:51Z (#1568 comment) | #1468 | run [38267190833](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38267190833) (head `d9b302c6b4d7`, green 15:01Z) | `265cec3014449d6c32fe7d15cad4403d4fb346eb` — equal on both |

gh-1537 AC5's tree-coverage intent was already implemented — the guard passes `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` and `decide()` compares it against each dispatch run's head tree. Two wiring bugs killed it.

## Mechanism (two bugs, both in `fetch_validated_runs`)

1. **Wrong jq path.** Each run's tree was resolved via `gh api repos/.../commits/<sha> --jq .tree.sha` — but the commits API has **no top-level `tree` key** (keys: `author, comments_url, commit, committer, files, html_url, node_id, parents, sha, stats, url`); the tree lives at `.commit.tree.sha`. The lookup returned empty, `tree_sha` stayed falsy, and the tree-match branch never fired → **every merge-commit landing alarmed** (only exact-SHA fast-forwards could pass).
2. **`conclusion` dropped from fetched runs.** `decide()` re-checks `run.get("conclusion") != "success"` on every run — a defensive re-check for the `--runs-json` test seam — but the fetch path never put `conclusion` in the dicts, so every live run read as `None != "success"` and was skipped → **the live path alarmed on every push**, even the fast-forward case. The Dart fixtures all carry `conclusion: 'success'`, which is why the test seam never saw it.

## Fix (surgical)

- `.tree.sha` → `.commit.tree.sha` (+ `or None` normalization)
- propagate `conclusion` into fetched run dicts
- the alarm body's "considered runs" lines now render each run's **resolved tree** alongside the head sha, so future alarms are self-diagnosing

## Live verification (read-only, post-fix)

## Description

## The false alarms

- **AC5** tree-lookup failure (commit API 404) → warning + alarm, never a false validate

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1537 AC5 SM
+# merge guard (sm_merge_guard.py), gh-1568.
+#

+#   AC1 (the gh-1568 regression) a merge-commit landing whose tree equals
+#       a successful dispatch's commit tree VALIDATES — with the commits
+#       API served in its REAL shape (tree nested under `commit`, no
+#       top-level `tree` key). The shipped `.tree.sha` jq path resolved
+#       empty for every run, so every merge-commit landing false-alarmed
+#       (issue #1568: merges 392fe540ae of #1484 and afed64bfd0 of #1468
+#       both carried trees byte-identical to their green validations).
+#   AC2 an UNCOVERED tree still alarms (exit 3) — the fix must not mute
+#       the invariant.
+#   AC3 a fast-forward landing (pushed sha == validated head sha)
+#       validates with no tree lookup at all.
+#   AC4 the race: a validation still in_progress at push time can never
+#       certify — alarm (the SM merges strictly after green, so
+#       in_progress-at-push means the merge beat the validation).
+#   AC5 a failed tree lookup (commit API 404) degrades to a warning and
+#       alarms — never a false validate, never a traceback.
+#   AC6 the alarm body renders each considered run's resolved tree, so
+#       future alarms are self-diagnosing, and files with the
+#       bug+sm-guard labels (dedup convention untouched).
+# Same discipline as check_lockfiles_selftest.sh (#1100 pattern).
+set -u
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+GUARD="$HERE/sm_merge_guard.py"
+TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap '[ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

+fails=0
+check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+check_absent() { # check_absent <desc> <grep-exit-code: 1 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" != "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi

+

+PUSHED_TREE=0fd92616c897199580c030675dd7854758ea9879
+HEAD_SHA=06898ec2b58c5a22696b7b2e2f147d6fab976c5a
+SUBJECT=[REDACTED:Certificate DN]
+NOW="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
+
+# Canned gh: case-dispatch on argv. The commits fixture uses the REAL
+# response shape — `commit.tree.sha`, deliberately WITHOUT a top-level
+# `tree` key (that absence is exactly what broke `.tree.sha`).
+mkdir -p "$TMP/bin" "$TMP/stub"
+cat > "$TMP/bin/gh" <<STUB
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -u
+case "\$*" in
+  *"run list"*) cat "$TMP/stub/runs.json" ;;
+  *"issue list"*) echo "" ;; # post-jq: .[0].number // empty on no match
+  *"issue create"*)

+    prev=""
+    for a in "\$@"; do

+print(json.load(sys.stdin)["commit"]["tree"]["sha"])'
+    else

+      exit 1
+    fi ;;
+  *) echo "stub gh: unexpected call: \$*" >&2; exit 64 ;;
+esac

+ "commit": {"tree": {"sha": "$PUSHED_TREE"}},

+             {"sha": "6d7e0d268b02aee7e4961f14d09359fd5b1427d3"}]}
+JSON

+check "AC1 verdict cites the covering run by tree match" $?
+grep -q "Traceback" "$TMP/ac1.log"
+c…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SM merge guard (gh-1537 AC5) — the cheap alarm for the serialized-
validation invariant.

Invariant under watch: the SM queue (machine-sm.yml -> factory-sm) is
strictly serialized and validates the EXACT tree that merges — update
branch onto main, dispatch ci.yml on the updated head, merge only when
green. With the post-merge main CI run retired (gh-1537), nothing else
stands between a violated invariant and a red main: this guard fires on
every push to main and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a
SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch run (an SM pre-merge validation).

A push whose tree has no successful dispatched validation is the
#687-invariant violation the owner asked to alarm on instead of relying
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard —
defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full
quality gate that runs on the cut v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ALARM_LABEL = "sm-guard"
# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, window_hours: int) -> list:
    """Recent SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch runs, each with the tree
    sha of its head commit resolved via the commits API."""
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", "ci.yml",
             "--event", "workflow_dispatch",
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append({
            "database_id": r["databaseId"],
            "head_sha": r["headSha"],
            # decide() re-checks conclusion on every run; without the
            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below
            "created_at": r["createdAt"],
        })
    # Newest first — the match is almost always the first lookup.
    for run in runs[:MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS]:
        try:
            # The commits API nests the tree under `commit` — `.tree.sha`
            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()
            run["tree_sha"] = tree or None
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    return runs


def decide(subject: str, pushed_sha: str, pushed_tree: str,
           runs: list) -> dict:
    """The pure invariant check. `runs` carry head_sha/tree_sha of
    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
        return {"verdict": "skipped",
                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
    for run in runs:
        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
        # invariant holds by construction).
        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
                              f"commit re-landed it)"}
    return {"verdict": "alarm",
            "reason": "no successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run covers "
                      "this tree — the SM merged without (or before) a "
                      "green validation of the exact tree"}


def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
                runs: list) -> None:
    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
    links = "\n".join(
        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
        + ")"
        for r in runs[:10])
    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
    body = (
        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
    if existing.strip():
        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
           "--body", body)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: commented on #{existing.strip()}")
    else:
        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push would skip the guard (defense-in-depth —
# gh-1522 retired the bump flow, so none land anymore; if one ever
# returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the v* tag run's full
# quality gate BEFORE publish/binaries). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Pin to the SAME frozen identity PUSHED_SHA uses
          # (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha): the tree under
          # assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD, so an unpinned
          # checkout could drift to a moved main and have run-for-push-A
          # certify a newer push B's tree it never examined (same lesson
          # as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin,
          # #1178 — gh-1522 folded tag cutting back into the release job).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --alarm-issue

## PR Description

## The false alarms

Two sm-guard alarms in 49 minutes, both on SM train merges whose trees were **proven byte-identical** to their green validations:

| push (main) | merge of | validated by | proven identical tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| `392fe540ae73` @14:43:44Z (#1568 body) | #1484 | run [38260860862](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38260860862) (head `06898ec2b58c`, green 14:09Z) | `0fd92616c897199580c030675dd7854758ea9879` — `git rev-parse '<sha>^{tree}'` equal on both |
| `afed64bfd07a` @15:30:51Z (#1568 comment) | #1468 | run [38267190833](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38267190833) (head `d9b302c6b4d7`, green 15:01Z) | `265cec3014449d6c32fe7d15cad4403d4fb346eb` — equal on both |

gh-1537 AC5's tree-coverage intent was already implemented — the guard passes `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` and `decide()` compares it against each dispatch run's head tree. Two wiring bugs killed it.

## Mechanism (two bugs, both in `fetch_validated_runs`)

1. **Wrong jq path.** Each run's tree was resolved via `gh api repos/.../commits/<sha> --jq .tree.sha` — but the commits API has **no top-level `tree` key** (keys: `author, comments_url, commit, committer, files, html_url, node_id, parents, sha, stats, url`); the tree lives at `.commit.tree.sha`. The lookup returned empty, `tree_sha` stayed falsy, and the tree-match branch never fired → **every merge-commit landing alarmed** (only exact-SHA fast-forwards could pass).
2. **`conclusion` dropped from fetched runs.** `decide()` re-checks `run.get("conclusion") != "success"` on every run — a defensive re-check for the `--runs-json` test seam — but the fetch path never put `conclusion` in the dicts, so every live run read as `None != "success"` and was skipped → **the live path alarmed on every push**, even the fast-forward case. The Dart fixtures all carry `conclusion: 'success'`, which is why the test seam never saw it.

## Fix (surgical)

- `.tree.sha` → `.commit.tree.sha` (+ `or None` normalization)
- propagate `conclusion` into fetched run dicts
- the alarm body's "considered runs" lines now render each run's **resolved tree** alongside the head sha, so future alarms are self-diagnosing

## Live verification (read-only, post-fix)

- merge `392fe540ae73` / tree `0fd92616…` → `ok — tree match: run 38260860862 validated this exact tree` (exit 0)
- merge `afed64bfd07a` / tree `265cec30…` → `ok — tree match: run 38267190833 validated this exact tree` (exit 0)
- synthetic uncovered tree → alarm, exit 3 (the invariant still bites)

## Offline test matrix — `scripts/sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh` (16 checks, wired into ci.yml)

PATH-stubbed `gh` serving the **real** commits-API response shape (tree nested under `commit`, no top-level `tree`), real shas from the #1484 false alarm:

- **AC1** (regression) merge-commit landing with identical tree validates; verdict cites the covering run
- **AC2** uncovered tree → alarm, exit 3
- **AC3** fast-forward (pushed sha == validated head) validates, no tree lookup needed (fixture 404s)
- **AC4** race: a validation still `in_progress` at push time can never certify → alarm
- **AC5** tree-lookup failure (commit API 404) → warning + alarm, never a false validate
- **AC6** alarm body renders considered runs' resolved trees and files with `bug`+`sm-guard` labels (dedup convention untouched)

## Race decision (AC4): alarm stands, no wait/recheck

The invariant is "validated **before** merge"; only a completed-success run certifies. The SM merges strictly after green, so a run still in progress at push time means the merge beat its validation — that *is* the violation. A recheck-wait would contradict the guard's design (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly not a polling backstop) and would delay-then-mask real violations; the deduplicated issue keeps the evidence if the run lands green afterward.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: both fixes + self-diagnosing alarm body + fixture selftest in CI. Unchanged by design: 24h window, `MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS=40`, release-bump skip, alarm dedup/labels.

Fixes #1568

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1537 AC5 SM
+# merge guard (sm_merge_guard.py), gh-1568.
+#
+# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no real runs):
+#   AC1 (the gh-1568 regression) a merge-commit landing whose tree equals
+#       a successful dispatch's commit tree VALIDATES — with the commits
+#       API served in its REAL shape (tree nested under `commit`, no
+#       top-level `tree` key). The shipped `.tree.sha` jq path resolved
+#       empty for every run, so every merge-commit landing false-alarmed

+#       both carried trees byte-identical to their green validations).
+#   AC2 an UNCOVERED tree still alarms (exit 3) — the fix must not mute
+#       the invariant.
+#   AC3 a fast-forward landing (pushed sha == validated head sha)
+#       validates with no tree lookup at all.
+#   AC4 the race: a validation still in_progress at push time can never
+#       certify — alarm (the SM merges strictly after green, so
+#       in_progress-at-push means the merge beat the validation).
+#   AC5 a failed tree lookup (commit API 404) degrades to a warning and
+#       alarms — never a false validate, never a traceback.
+#   AC6 the alarm body renders each considered run's resolved tree, so
+#       future alarms are self-diagnosing, and files with the
+#       bug+sm-guard labels (dedup convention untouched).
+# Same discipline as check_lockfiles_selftest.sh (#1100 pattern).
+set -u
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+GUARD="$HERE/sm_merge_guard.py"
+TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap '[ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
+
+fails=0
+check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}
+check_absent() { # check_absent <desc> <grep-exit-code: 1 = pass>
+  if [ "$2" != "0" ]; then
+    echo "  ok: $1"
+  else
+    echo "  FAIL: $1"
+    fails=$((fails + 1))
+  fi
+}

+# (same as test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart's Process.run('python3')).
+run_guard() { python3 "$GUARD" "$@"; }
+

+PUSHED_TREE=0fd92616c897199580c030675dd7854758ea9879
+HEAD_SHA=06898ec2b58c5a22696b7b2e2f147d6fab976c5a
+SUBJECT=[REDACTED:Certificate DN]
+NOW="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
+
+# Canned gh: case-dispatch on argv. The commits fixture uses the REAL
+# response shape — `commit.tree.sha`, deliberately WITHOUT a top-level
+# `tree` key (that absence is exactly what broke `.tree.sha`).
+mkdir -p "$TMP/bin" "$TMP/stub"
+cat > "$TMP/bin/gh" <<STUB
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -u
+case "\$*" in
+  *"run list"*) cat "$TMP/stub/runs.json" ;;
+  *"issue list"*) echo "" ;; # post-jq: .[0].number // empty on no match
+  *"issue create"*)
+    printf '%s\n' "\$*" > "$TMP/stub/create_args.log"
+    prev=""
+    for a in "\$@"; do

+  *"repos/"*"/commits/"*)

+    if [ -f "$TMP/stub/commit-\$sha.json" ]; then

+      # the guard uses (the whole point of the gh-1568 regression is
+      # that the filter runs against the REAL response shape).
+      cat "$TMP/stub/commit-\$sha.json" | python3 -c '
+import json, sys
+print(json.load(sys.stdin)["commit"]["tree"]["sha"])'
+    else
+      echo "gh: HTTP 404: no commit \$sha" >&2
+      exit 1
+    fi ;;
+  *) echo "stub gh: unexpected call: \$*" >&2; exit 64 ;;
+esac
+STUB

+export PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH"
+
+# One successful dispatch on HEAD_SHA, recently inside the 24h window.
+cat > "$TMP/stub/runs.json" <<JSON
+[{"databaseId": 38260860862, "headSha": "$HEAD_SHA",
+  "conclusion": "success", "createdAt": "$NOW"}]
+JSON

+{"sha": "$HEAD_SHA",
+ "commit": {"tree": {"sha": "$PUSHED_TREE"}},
+ "parents": [{"sha": "4b7a740d990636c6db769eb3ec83b58bee1a4c06"},
+             {"sha": "6d7e0d268b02aee7e4961f14d09359fd5b1427d3"}]}
+JSON
+

+out="$(run_guard --repo acme/widget --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
+  --subject "$SUBJECT" --tree "$PUSHED_TREE" 2>&1)"
+check "AC1 merge-commit landing with identical tree validates (exit 0)" $?
+printf '%s\n' "$out" > "$TMP/ac1.log"
+grep -q "tree match: run 38260860862" "$TMP/ac1.log"
+check "AC1 verdict cites the covering run by tree match" $?
+grep -q "Traceback" "$TMP/ac1.log"
+c…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +

   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —

and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SM merge guard (gh-1537 AC5) — the cheap alarm for the serialized-
validation invariant.

Invariant under watch: the SM queue (machine-sm.yml -> factory-sm) is
strictly serialized and validates the EXACT tree that merges — update
branch onto main, dispatch ci.yml on the updated head, merge only when
green. With the post-merge main CI run retired (gh-1537), nothing else
stands between a violated invariant and a red main: this guard fires on
every push to main and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a
SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch run (an SM pre-merge validation).

A push whose tree has no successful dispatched validation is the
#687-invariant violation the owner asked to alarm on instead of relying
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard —
defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full
quality gate that runs on the cut v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ALARM_LABEL = "sm-guard"
# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, window_hours: int) -> list:
    """Recent SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch runs, each with the tree
    sha of its head commit resolved via the commits API."""
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", "ci.yml",
             "--event", "workflow_dispatch",
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append({
            "database_id": r["databaseId"],
            "head_sha": r["headSha"],
            # decide() re-checks conclusion on every run; without the
            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below
            "created_at": r["createdAt"],
        })
    # Newest first — the match is almost always the first lookup.
    for run in runs[:MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS]:
        try:
            # The commits API nests the tree under `commit` — `.tree.sha`
            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()
            run["tree_sha"] = tree or None
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    return runs


def decide(subject: str, pushed_sha: str, pushed_tree: str,
           runs: list) -> dict:
    """The pure invariant check. `runs` carry head_sha/tree_sha of
    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
        return {"verdict": "skipped",
                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
    for run in runs:
        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
        # invariant holds by construction).
        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
                              f"commit re-landed it)"}
    return {"verdict": "alarm",
            "reason": "no successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run covers "
                      "this tree — the SM merged without (or before) a "
                      "green validation of the exact tree"}


def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
                runs: list) -> None:
    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
    links = "\n".join(
        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
        + ")"
        for r in runs[:10])
    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
    body = (
        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
    if existing.strip():
        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
           "--body", body)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: commented on #{existing.strip()}")
    else:
        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push would skip the guard (defense-in-depth —
# gh-1522 retired the bump flow, so none land anymore; if one ever
# returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the v* tag run's full
# quality gate BEFORE publish/binaries). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Pin to the SAME frozen identity PUSHED_SHA uses
          # (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha): the tree under
          # assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD, so an unpinned
          # checkout could drift to a moved main and have run-for-push-A
          # certify a newer push B's tree it never examined (same lesson
          # as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin,
          # #1178 — gh-1522 folded tag cutting back into the release job).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --alarm-issue
